cellular.name: Cellular Networks
cellular.subtitle: 4G / 5G Mobile Communication
cellular.overview: Cellular networks divide geographic areas into cells, each served by a base station (cell tower). As users move between cells, their connection is handed off seamlessly. Modern 4G LTE and 5G networks provide high-speed data, voice, and multimedia services to billions of mobile users worldwide.
cellular.howItWorks: A mobile device communicates with the nearest base station via radio waves. The base station connects to the core network through backhaul links. When a user moves from one cell to another, the network performs a handover — transferring the active session to the new base station without dropping the connection. The core network handles routing, authentication, and connection to the internet or other networks.
keyFeatures: Wide-area coverage spanning cities and countries
High mobility support — works while traveling at high speeds
Supports voice calls, SMS, and high-speed data simultaneously
5G introduces ultra-low latency (< 1ms) and massive device density
Frequency bands: 700 MHz to 39 GHz (5G mmWave)

specs.Coverage Range: Up to 30 km per cell tower

layers.name: Core Network (EPC/5GC)
layers.desc: MME, SGW, PGW — handles routing & auth

satellite.name: Satellite Networks
satellite.subtitle: GEO, MEO & LEO Communication
satellite.overview: Satellite networks use orbiting satellites to relay communication signals across vast distances. They are essential for reaching remote areas where terrestrial infrastructure is impractical. Three orbital types serve different needs: GEO for broadcasting, MEO for navigation (GPS), and LEO for low-latency internet (Starlink).
satellite.howItWorks: A ground station (or user terminal) transmits a signal up to the satellite (uplink). The satellite amplifies and retransmits the signal back to Earth (downlink), either to another ground station or directly to user terminals. GEO satellites stay fixed relative to Earth at 35,786 km altitude, while LEO constellations orbit at 500-2000 km, requiring many satellites to maintain continuous coverage through orbital handovers.
keyFeatures: Global coverage including oceans, deserts, and polar regions
GEO provides fixed coverage with just 3 satellites for Earth
LEO constellations (Starlink) reduce latency to 20-40 ms
Critical for maritime, aviation, and disaster relief communication
Operates independently of ground infrastructure

specs.Frequency: L, S, C, Ku, Ka bands (1-40 GHz)

layers.name: User Terminal
layers.desc: Satellite phones, VSAT dishes, Starlink terminals

layers.name: Space Segment
layers.desc: Satellites in GEO (35,786 km), MEO (2,000-35,786 km), or LEO (500-2,000 km)

wifi.name: Wireless LAN (Wi-Fi)
wifi.subtitle: IEEE 802.11 Standards
wifi.overview: Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) enables devices to connect to a local area network wirelessly using the IEEE 802.11 family of standards. It operates through access points that bridge wireless devices to wired networks. Wi-Fi is the most widely used wireless technology for indoor connectivity in homes, offices, and public spaces.
wifi.howItWorks: An access point (AP) broadcasts a network identifier (SSID). Devices discover available networks and authenticate using protocols like WPA3. Once connected, data frames are transmitted over radio frequencies (2.4 GHz or 5 GHz). The MAC layer handles channel access using CSMA/CA to avoid collisions. In infrastructure mode, all traffic routes through the AP. In ad-hoc mode, devices communicate directly peer-to-peer.
keyFeatures: Very high speeds — Wi-Fi 6 supports up to 9.6 Gbps
Low latency (< 5 ms) ideal for real-time applications
Two modes: Infrastructure (via AP) and Ad-hoc (peer-to-peer)
Operates on 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E) bands
CSMA/CA for collision avoidance at the MAC layer

layers.desc: Bridges wireless and wired LAN segments

broadcast.name: Broadcast Networks
broadcast.subtitle: Radio, Television & Digital Broadcasting
broadcast.overview: Broadcast networks transmit signals from a single source to many receivers simultaneously — a one-to-many communication model. This includes AM/FM radio, analog/digital television, and modern digital audio broadcasting (DAB). Unlike two-way networks, broadcast is inherently unidirectional, making it efficient for mass content delivery.
broadcast.howItWorks: A broadcast transmitter converts audio/video content into electromagnetic signals and radiates them via high-power antennas. The signals propagate through the atmosphere and are received by antennas on consumer devices (radios, TVs). AM uses amplitude modulation on medium-wave frequencies for long range. FM uses frequency modulation on VHF for higher quality audio. Digital TV (DVB) encodes content as digital data, enabling HD video and multiple channels per frequency.
keyFeatures: One-to-many transmission — efficient for mass media delivery
Very large coverage area from a single transmitter
No per-user cost — free to receive with appropriate antenna
AM radio can cover thousands of kilometers (ground wave)
Digital broadcasting (DVB/DAB) supports HD quality and data services

layers.name: Receiver Devices
layers.desc: Radios, televisions, set-top boxes, car receivers
